overall: Atlanta has already peaked at 89.6°F around 12:50 ET and has since dropped notably to 82.4°F by 15:05 ET — a 7.2°F decline in roughly two hours — suggesting convective activity, cloud cover, or outflow boundaries have suppressed afternoon heating. The velocity of +0.0°F/hr at 15:05 confirms the temperature is no longer rising, and the dewpoint of 75.2°F indicates an oppressively humid airmass that likely fueled midday convection responsible for the cooling. The day has trended cooler than most NWP guidance expected by mid-afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS, ECMWF, and HRRR cluster tightly at 89.9–90.3°F, while NBM at 87.5°F has already been busted upward by the observed 89.6°F running max. The even ensemble model (Tier 1, 58% confidence) targets 90–91°F, which aligns well with the three-model NWP consensus, but the observed afternoon temperature collapse makes reaching that range very unlikely from here.
max_temp_prediction: With the current temperature sitting 7.2°F below the running max at 15:05 ET and zero upward velocity, the window for additional peak heating is effectively closed — it is past the typical daily heating maximum and convective cloud cover appears to be limiting recovery. The daily high will almost certainly be the already-observed 89.6°F; a marginal touch of 90°F cannot be fully ruled out if skies briefly clear before 16:00 ET, but the probability is low given the sustained temperature suppression. Confidence is high that the final TMAX lands in the 89.5–90.0°F range, anchored near the current running max.
